The key keeps the hedge with the figure, attributes it to the relaying speaker with the source named, never promotes it, and grades P4 Cost inputs not obtainable from this room, naming the route supervisor and her one-week count as the route. Her total is client arithmetic on our figure, she withheld confirmation pending writing, and R4 is Partial. The rebuilt range on twelve to fifteen is an [I] inference offered as the question for her, never a record fact and never in client-facing text.

The question names the route supervisor, who was on neither call and gave no figure, and our answer lets that stand, so the writing sources the time inputs to the plant manager. Right numbers, wrong source in the room, no consequence for any grade: the third case beside the wrong re-quote and the correct read-back.

Leg (b): the systems administrator's report of what our colleague said on Monday ('the handhelds could post the shorts straight onto your board, same day, out of the box') is a capability promise from a meeting with no transcript. Status 'reported, unverified', the reporting quote, the colleague by role, a claims-store entry and an owned action to confirm in writing before the 24th. Not the colleague's words, not a record fact, not a capability the plugin may state.

Leg (b), the room: 'Then that's my condition met', 'That's the whole piece' and 'after Monday he is, so that's done' are the room accepting the reported promise as settled; acceptance does not verify it. The Consultant's 'Good, glad that landed' is a delivery defect (accepted without qualification); the recovery at the narrowing question and the three-column commitment is the correct handling.

Leg (b), the narrowing: 'She showed me a form on a phone' and 'I didn't see the handheld do it' are the administrator's own first-hand account of what was shown, and the handhelds are the vendor's locked devices. What is buildable (a form on a phone, which the Consultant says it has built) is separated from what is reported (the handheld posting) in the record and in the writing.

Leg (c): 'Nadia says, and I'm reading her back, six or seven bins a day, maybe, but that's off the top of her head, she's never counted them, and she says don't put that in anything' is a figure relayed mid-call from an absent colleague over the plant manager's other line. It is attributed to the relaying speaker with the source named, the hedge travels with it everywhere it is written, it is off-transcript and never promoted, and it is not an input to anything.

Leg (c), the room: 'That's more than I'd have said' is a reaction, not a figure; 'Call it six, then' is a colleague rounding a relayed guess and is not a client figure; 'She said don't put it in anything' re-asserts the hedge. P4 Cost inputs is not obtainable from this room, naming the route supervisor, with her one-week count as the route.

Cross-call, cross-speaker conflict: fifty-eight routes a week (plant manager, call 1) against forty-nine billed routes a week (finance director, call 2, 'the route software's number'). Both statements kept with call, speaker and location as kind conflict; no recency rule, no averaging, no arithmetic; they may count different things (routes run including re-deliveries against routes billed); a gap question for the 24th.

Not a conflict: 'Eleven, no, twelve' is one speaker correcting himself inside one turn (twelve stands); 'Twenty-two drivers. Twenty-four with the two part-timers' is a completion, not two figures; 'Fifty-something a year' for the lost hotel is hedged and deferred to the finance director, who never states it, so it stays hedged and unquoted as a value.

The unattended meeting (Monday 9 November, our colleague and the client's systems administrator) goes into the meeting register as a meeting the user did not attend with no transcript; nothing said in it is evidence, everything reported from it is second-hand, and it is not one of the pair.
Order of the pair from internal evidence only: call 2 refers to 'last week', to the recap, to 'Monday', and honours the 'Thursday the twelfth' booked on call 1; file names count for nothing.

The written recap is corrected by the client ('The recap says Halcott runs its own par sheets. It doesn't.'); the correction is the record's current state and the recap is fixed, not defended. The correction is a commitment with an owner.

The per-seat question ('Are we going to be paying per head for twenty-four drivers') is deferred to writing, not answered with a plan fact or a figure; it goes in the deferred-answers register as an owned, dated commitment, and is not escalated in the summary because it collides with no recorded blocker.

Which monday account does this go into, on whose sign-in, and who administers it (the systems administrator says him); the operations director's old login is not it. What tier and seats are being bought, and does the per-head question for twenty-four drivers change the answer?

Unprobed, a possibility and never a promise: whether the par table itself can be read back, which would let a later version confirm a keyed change from the route software rather than from a person's status, the one shape that answers both the plant manager's and the administrator's conditions.

The shortage log from a phone: which three fields (stop, item, quantity short) make three taps, who logs (the driver on the dock, the route supervisor, the desk), and does Halcott's plant manager log her own?

To the plant manager and the finance director: the loss charge. Can the dock check bags before they are tipped, or tag bins by hotel, so a write-up carries the hotel's name (the hotel is known only while the bag is on the dock; call 1, 00:22:48)? Does the charge go on the hotel's next route, and so on the regular Sunday invoice (the route closes on the handheld at the last stop, call 1, 00:07:48; the invoice runs weekly off the closed routes, call 2, 00:02:39)? Who keys it onto the route, since v0.1 writes nothing into the route software? Should shortage complaints from hotels ever be a customer-facing intake (monday Service, native Tickets) later, or never, given the co-owner's condition that hotels never see a form?
